posts.topic: VALUE-FIRST cold-reader acquisition post (canon 4c40c22 / LOOP_PROTOCOL §9 top-level subsection), NOT an experiment diary. Rationale from hard evidence read this run (Day 12): the Day-11 top-level post carried an INLINE external link and a meta Day-N-diary hook, and got only 4 impressions (owner's own link-free posts historically 46-143), though 2 of those 4 clicked (50% CTR). Two evidence-based fixes applied at once: (1) the main tweet is now standalone-VALUABLE to any ChatGPT user (teaches the product's real differentiator -- the anti-hallucination 'don't invent facts / write I will confirm and follow up' constraint) with NO diary framing, so a cold reader gets value with zero prior context; (2) the main tweet carries NO external link (X throttles link-in-post reach) -- the link to the FREE JP guide (a better JP-matched offer than the EN $19 store) is moved to a self-reply. This tests whether owned-account top-level reach recovers toward the 46-143 baseline when the post is value-first and link-free, while giving engaged readers a real conversion path to the free lead magnet. Genuinely new vs both prior posts (different content type, different destination, different structure); not a rehash.

posts.observation_plan: Read main-tweet impressions + reply url_link_clicks at ~+24h (Day-13) via x-verify-reply.yml (X_TWEET_ID=2098569637827141687 for reach; X_TWEET_ID=2098569639416721518 for the reply's url_link_clicks). Compare reach vs Day-11's link-inline post (4 impressions): recovery toward 46-143 supports the link-suppression + value-first hypothesis; still ~4 means owned-account top-level reach itself is near-zero regardless of format (then pivot off X).
